title: Multiple NFL Teams Eye Jonathan Taylor Trade, NBC Sports Confirms
body:
The NFL trade market is already buzzing with speculation that the Indianapolis Colts could move their former first‑overall pick, Jonathan Taylor, before the deadline. According to multiple league insiders, several franchises — ranging from perennial contenders to emerging playoff hopefuls — have expressed concrete interest in acquiring the 25‑year‑old running back, whose production has been hampered by injuries and a stagnant offensive line. While the Colts have not confirmed any intent to part ways with Taylor, the growing chatter has ignited a debate about whether the team will become a seller at the trade deadline or hold onto its marquee asset in hopes of a late‑season surge.

Taylor entered the 2023 season as a centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense, but a series of nagging injuries limited him to just 560 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns through ten games. The Colts’ offensive line, plagued by injuries and inconsistent play, has struggled to open lanes, forcing the team to rely heavily on short passes and play‑action that often fall short against elite defenses. As a result, the Colts sit near the bottom of the league in rushing yards per game, a stark contrast to the 1,811 yards Taylor amassed in his rookie campaign. The decline has prompted front‑office personnel to reassess his value, especially as the trade deadline looms and the market for top‑tier backs remains thin.

Among the suitors, the New England Patriots, Miami Dolphins and Denver Broncos have surfaced most frequently in reports. The Patriots, still seeking a reliable workhorse to complement their passing attack, view Taylor as a potential upgrade over their current backfield rotation. Miami, on the other hand, is looking to add depth after a season‑ending injury to their starting running back, while Denver hopes to pair Taylor with its dynamic receiving corps to create a more balanced offense. Each club is believed to be preparing offers that could include a combination of mid‑round draft picks and a veteran player, though exact terms remain under negotiation. The Colts, who have already moved on veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. in a separate trade, are now weighing whether the return on Taylor would outweigh the risk of losing a player who could still produce at a high level if healthy.

The decision is further complicated by Indianapolis’ broader strategic outlook. Head coach Shane Steichen, who was hired after the dismissal of former coach Frank Reich, has been tasked with rebuilding a roster that struggled to find consistency under the previous regime. While the Colts have a young quarterback in Anthony Richardson who shows flashes of brilliance, the team’s overall depth remains questionable. Trading Taylor could free up cap space and acquire assets to bolster the offensive line, defensive secondary, or future draft capital, aligning with a longer‑term rebuild. Conversely, retaining Taylor provides a proven weapon that could help the Colts stay competitive in a tight AFC South and potentially secure a playoff berth, a goal that would appease an impatient fan base still reeling from recent coaching turnover.

Analysts also note that the market for elite running backs has shifted dramatically over the past decade, with teams increasingly reluctant to invest heavily in a position that traditionally offers a shorter career span. This trend makes any trade involving a player of Taylor’s caliber all the more significant. If the Colts can secure a package that includes a high‑value draft pick, they would join a select group of franchises that have successfully leveraged a star running back for future flexibility. However, the risk remains that a deal could fall through, leaving Indianapolis with a disgruntled player and limited options heading into the final stretch of the season.

As the deadline approaches, the Colts’ front office will need to balance immediate competitiveness with long‑term sustainability. Should a satisfactory offer materialize, Indianapolis could pivot toward a rebuilding timeline, using the assets to address glaring needs on both sides of the ball. If not, the team will likely retain Taylor, hoping that a healthier Richardson and an improved offensive line can unlock his upside before the season’s end. Either scenario will shape the Colts’ trajectory for the next few years, and fans will be watching closely to see whether the franchise chooses to gamble on a potential resurgence or to cash in on a once‑a‑year talent before his market value wanes.
